text:
jess (release): Kicking off the py/ts SDK publish in the 6pm change window. Plan: canary -> staggered canary -> full. Deprecation note for legacy sync client goes live with the release. Any last blockers?
anna (devex): ack. I updated the release notes draft and added the migration snippet. ping @leo for docs link updates. :white_check_mark:
leo (docs): on it, will push the migration page and add the code example. ETA 30m.
mike (infra): preflight: build infra smoke passed on canaries. Autosigner queue length is okay. I'll trigger canary once jess gives go.
jess (release): go from me. deploy-bot, start canary for py@2.3.0-canary and ts@1.9.0-canary.
deploy-bot: Started canary deploy: py@2.3.0-canary -> 3 nodes, ts@1.9.0-canary -> 4 nodes. Logs: https://ci.redwood/rel/1767894321/logs
anna (devex): quick note: we pinned the legacy sync client deprecation to 90 days in the notes. Also adding an inline snippet: ```pip install redwood-sdk==2.3.0``` and `npm install @redwood/sdk@1.9.0`.
jess (release): saw a failing integration on the python canary: test_integration_auth failing intermittently. Retrying.
mike (infra): saw OOMs on the py canary container at the same time. Increasing memory for canary nodes and retrying.
deploy-bot: Canary retry completed. py canary health: degraded (1 failing node), ts canary healthy.
jess (release): given the regression and OOM traces, I'm going to pause the full rollout. Do we want to rollback the py canary to py@2.2.7 and unpin the deprecation publish until we confirm?
anna (devex): +1 on rollback. We should also pin the package index tags so users on the canary channel don't get stuck. I'll prepare rollback notes.
leo (docs): pausing docs publish that references 2.3.0 until we confirm. Will change docs branch to draft.
mike (infra): rolling back py canary to 2.2.7 now. Also capturing heap dump and the container logs: `gs://redwood-logs/releases/1767894321/py-canary/*`.
deploy-bot: Rollback complete: py@2.2.7 restored on canary nodes. Canary health: healthy.
jess (release): thanks. Action items: 1) rollback final publish of py/ts packages (if already promoted to registry) — we didn't promote, good. 2) run debug runbook on OOMs tomorrow AM. 3) keep deprecation note in draft until after stability.
anna (devex): I'll update the release checklist and mark 'deprecation publish' HOLD. Also will create a short postmortem thread for the canary failure.
leo (docs): docs branch set to draft. Will re-open PR after fix.
jess (release): rough timeline: Monday morning we run extended canary with memory bump, if green we'll proceed with full publish and lift deprecation hold. If not, escalate to infra/rls triage. Thanks everyone. :pray:
mike (infra): noted. Adding a guard in the publish job to block deprecation publish until `release-hold` flag is cleared.
anna (devex): leaving a short note for customers in the release-notes draft so it's not accidentally published: "Release held due to canary instability; deprecation will be announced after follow-up."
jess (release): closing thread for now. I'll post an update when we have Monday results. :eyes:
